title: an ordinary callback argument that cannot fail is untouched by the callback-contract rule
notes: The plainest over-correction guard in the family: the same consumer, the same object-literal argument position, the same loose parameter type, and a callback with no failure at all. Every refusal in this family is charged on the callback's inferred failure set being non-empty, so a rule that charged on POSITION rather than on the value's channel would refuse this program too. It runs.
